references.text: The preceding verse establishes the context of the Sabbath year's produce as food for everyone, including the master, servants, and foreigners.
The provision of the Sabbath year that the poor and the beasts of the field shall eat what grows on its own in the seventh year.
The command that the ox which treads out grain shall not have its mouth muzzled, showing God's care for animals and their right to food.
The psalm praises God who causes grass to grow for the cattle and plants for human service, demonstrating God's providence for both animals and people.
God gives food to all living creatures in due time and satisfies every living thing with what it desires.
God provides for the ravens when they cry out and their young wander about without food, showing God's care for all creation.
Jesus teaches about the birds that neither sow nor reap, yet the heavenly Father still gives them food, illustrating God's providence.
